text:
Spatial picking index landed. PickIndex (new, private[interaction]): uniform grid over target bounds boxes, built once in the PickingPlan constructor (forces the lazy per-target bounds at compile). Queries (hits, nearest via hits, select) collect a conservative candidate set from grid cells and run the exact geometric predicates unchanged on that subset; identical sort keys mean identical results. Soundness argument documented on the class: every finite-distance boundary piece/interior point of a clipped target lies within its unclipped source bounds, so a box filter expanded by tolerance + 1e-6 safety (> geometry epsilon 1e-8) can never drop a true hit. Plans with <= 16 bounded targets skip the grid. Targets with no bounds have no geometry and can match nothing; excluded outright.

Semantics preserved by proof and by oracle: hitsExhaustive/selectExhaustive (the pre-index scans) retained as private[interaction] test oracles; new dense-plan tests (578 targets: 24x24 disc lattice + 2 scene-spanning polylines + clipped rotated disc) compare ~4300 point queries across 5 tolerances and 15 area queries across all three AreaRules — all identical. Full interaction suite 53/53 JVM, 51/51 JS.

Measured on the 20k-mark faceted plan (receipt regenerated): hits 6449 -> 24.4 us/query median (~265x, alloc 9.5 MB -> ~30 KB per query), nearest 5678 -> 45 us, select rectangle 458 -> 42 ms (real candidate work dominates), pick-compile 21 -> 53 ms one-time (index build + bounds forcing). Hover is now ~3 orders of magnitude under the 50 ms budget.

Docs: modules/interaction/README.md status + capacity paragraphs rewritten (no more "exhaustive"); docs/limits.md picking bullet updated with before/after.
